paper.title: Sharper Regret Bounds for Time-Varying Gaussian Process Bandits with Constant Exploration

settings.name_in_paper: Time-varying Gaussian process (TV-GP) bandit with drift parameter epsilon
unmapped: reward function evolves by the Markov GP recursion f_{t+1} = sqrt(1-eps) f_t + sqrt(eps) g_{t+1}, with g_t i.i.d. GP(0,k_S) (separable time-decayed kernel)
the learner knows the drift parameter eps
derivative tail bound assumption (Assumption 1) on sample paths with constants a, b
settings.definition_quote: Let $(g_t)_{t\ge 1}$ be i.i.d.\ draws from $\mathcal{GP}(0,k_S)$ ... $f_1(x)=g_1(x),\qquad f_{t+1}(x)=\sqrt{1-\epsilon}\,f_t(x)+\sqrt{\epsilon}\,g_{t+1}(x)$ ... with drift parameter $\epsilon\in(0,1]$. ... $y_t = f_t(x_t) + z_t, z_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2)$ i.i.d. ... $r_t := f_t(x_t^\star)-f_t(x_t)$

symbols.beta_ucb: constant exploration parameter beta of GP-UCB
symbols.gamma_tilde: time-varying maximum information gain under the time-decayed kernel
symbols.r_dom: side length r with S subset of [0,r]^d
symbols.a_tail: constant a of the derivative tail bound
symbols.b_tail: constant b of the derivative tail bound
symbols.tau: grid resolution analysis parameter (grid size tau^d)
symbols.mu_w: expected spatial span E[sup f_t - inf f_t]
symbols.sigma_w: sub-Gaussian variance proxy of the span W_t

conditions: S subset of [0,r]^d compact and convex
derivative tail bound (Assumption 1) with constants a>=1, b>0
tuning: delta in (0,1), tau in N+ analysis parameters

source.label: thrm:improved_regret
source.quote: If the evaluation points $\{x_t\}_{t=1}^T$ are selected according to Algorithm~\ref{alg:TV} with any constant exploration parameter satisfying $\beta \ge 2\Big(\log\!\big(\tfrac{6}{\delta}\big)+ d\log(\tau)\Big)$ then the expected cumulative regret satisfies $\mathbb{E}[R_T] \le \sqrt{C_1 T \beta\,\tilde{\gamma}_T}+ T C_2 + T\delta C_3$, ... $C_1=\frac{8}{\log(1+\sigma^{-2})}, C_2=\frac{rdb}{\tau} \sqrt{\log(\frac{3ad}{\delta})}, C_3=\mu_w+2\sigma_w\sqrt{2\log(e/\delta)}$.

results.notes: Expectation over GP prior and noise; regret against per-round maximiser (dynamic, Bayesian). Linear in T; algorithm does not use T.

symbols.omega: failure probability of the realized-regret bound

source.label: prop:realized_regret
source.quote: Assume the setting and parameter choices of Theorem~\ref{thrm:improved_regret}. For any target failure probability $\omega \in (0,1)$, the realized cumulative regret $R_T$ satisfies the following bound with probability at least $1-\omega$: $R_T \le U_T + \frac{T \delta C_3}{\omega}$.

results.notes: U_T = sqrt(C_1 T beta gamma_tilde) + T C_2. Probability over prior and noise; omega chosen post hoc.

symbols.eps_drift: drift parameter epsilon of the TV-GP model

source.label: cor:prescribed_confidence
source.quote: Fix $\omega\in(0,1)$ and choose $\delta=\omega\epsilon^{\alpha/2}, \tau=\lceil\epsilon^{-\alpha/2}\rceil$, together with the constant exploration parameter $\beta=2(\log\frac{6}{\omega\epsilon^{\alpha/2}}+d\log\lceil\epsilon^{-\alpha/2}\rceil)$. Then, with probability at least $1-\omega$, $\frac{R_T}{T}=\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\epsilon^{\alpha/2}\sqrt{1+\log(1/\omega)+\log(1/\epsilon)})$.

results.notes: Paper bounds average regret R_T/T; multiplied by T. Algorithm uses omega and eps to set beta.

symbols.q: capacity exponent with static gamma_N = O_tilde(N^q), q in [0,1)

conditions: static maximum information gain gamma_N = O_tilde(N^q), q in [0,1)
tuning: delta = eps^(alpha/2), tau = ceil(eps^(-alpha/2)) with alpha = 2(1-q)/(4-q); beta at threshold equality

source.label: eq:regret_main_rate
source.quote: In the persistent-drift regime where $T$ exceeds this effective block length, Corollary~\ref{cor:info_gain_scaling} gives ... Balancing the remaining terms in Theorem~\ref{thrm:improved_regret} as in Section~\ref{subsec:Opt_beta_eps} then yields $\frac{\mathbb E[R_T]}{T}=\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\epsilon^{\frac{1-q}{4-q}})$.

results.notes: Derived in text from Theorem 1 + Corollary 7 rather than a numbered theorem. Average regret multiplied by T. Specialisations: squared exponential kernel gives T*eps^(1/4); Matern(nu>2) gives T*eps^(2nu/(8nu+3d)).
